With the exploit, an attacker could join or host a meeting and run malicious code on victims' devices, allowing them to steal data, turn on the camera or microphone, or install malware. Days before we spoke, OpenAI revealed it had produced the solutions to 10 long-standing mathematics problems, some of which had confounded academics for decades. summary: OpenAI is developing a smart speaker that uses moving parts to appear more lifelike, with a recent report confirming the device's existence and uniqueness. The speaker's design is intended to make it seem more alive. OpenAI has assured that the device is not a copy of existing products.

title: Suno hopes to go legit with watermarks for AI-generated music
content: Suno plans watermarks and download limits to stop "large-scale abuse."
summary: Suno is implementing watermarks and download limits to prevent large-scale abuse of AI-generated music, aiming to legitimize its service. This move targets users who exploit AI music generation for commercial gain. The new measures will help Suno comply with copyright laws.

title: Hank Green found the AI problem that YouTube labels can’t catch
content: "Slop" isn't the only problem.
summary: Hank Green discovered an issue with AI on YouTube that the platform's labels cannot detect, referring to it as a problem beyond 'slop'

title: Google plans to kill Assistant on your phone on September 4
content: Assistant will disappear, leaving only Gemini for voice control in the coming weeks.
summary: Google plans to discontinue Assistant on phones, replacing it with Gemini for voice control, starting September 4. This change will likely impact how users interact with their devices. The reason for the switch was not specified in the report.

title: XRP, ether lead crypto losses as traders eye $70,000 bitcoin next
content: Bitcoin failed to hold $65,000 for a fourth day as an oil rally revived inflation worries before Wednesday's U.S. price data.
summary: Bitcoin failed to sustain the $65,000 mark for a fourth consecutive day, as XRP and Ether led overall cryptocurrency losses. This market downturn is attributed to rekindled inflation concerns stemming from an oil rally, ahead of upcoming U.S. price data.

title: Planned Amazon data center could become the biggest climate polluter in the US
content: AI has already had a significant impact on Amazon’s carbon emissions, which it reported were up 16% last year — the wrong direction for a company that pledged to eliminate its carbon emissions by 2040.
summary: Amazon is planning a new data center in Texas that will include an on-site power plant. This facility could reportedly become the single largest source of climate pollution in the United States.

title: FlightAware sues Kalshi over bets on flight cancellations
content: The flight-tracking company alleges Kalshi used its data and trademark without permission to settle contracts on canceled flights.
summary: FlightAware is suing Kalshi for using its data and trademark without permission to settle contracts on canceled flights. Kalshi allegedly used FlightAware's information to determine the outcome of bets on flight cancellations. This lawsuit highlights issues of data usage and intellectual property.

title: Bitcoin’s BIP-110 fork is 300 blocks behind BTC and six years from fixing itself
content: The breakaway chain has produced two blocks since splitting off on Saturday. Bitcoin has produced more than 300 in the same stretch.
summary: A Bitcoin fork, BIP-110, has produced only two blocks since splitting on Saturday, falling significantly behind the main Bitcoin chain which produced over 300 blocks. This breakaway chain is currently stalled and estimated to take six years to resolve its issues.

title: FlightAware sues Kalshi over flight cancellation data
content: The legal action against Kalshi focused on trademark infringement and injury to its reputation in addition to citing state authorities comparing the company’s contracts to gambling.
summary: FlightAware is suing Kalshi over trademark infringement and reputational damage, with authorities comparing Kalshi's contracts to gambling. The lawsuit also involves issues with flight cancellation data. This case may have implications for data usage and intellectual property in the tech industry.

title: Judge stays CFTC’s case against US soldier over prediction market bets
content: A New York judge granted a motion filed by US prosecutors in July to stay the CFTC’s civil case against Gannon Ken Van Dyke over making more than $400,000 on prediction markets.
summary: A US judge has stayed a civil case against Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who made over $400,000 on prediction markets. The case was brought by the CFTC and has been put on hold. Van Dyke is a US soldier.

title: FlightAware sues Kalshi over alleged unauthorized data use for flight cancellation markets
content: FlightAware is also seeking a temporary restraining order to bar Kalshi from activities involving the flight-tracking site.
summary: FlightAware is suing Kalshi for allegedly using its data without permission to operate flight cancellation markets. FlightAware is seeking a temporary restraining order to stop Kalshi's activities. The lawsuit involves the use of flight-tracking data.

title: How ideas of a vast censorship network moved from the online fringe to Trump policy
content: This article was produced in partnership with Type Investigations, with support from the Wayne Barrett Project. One morning in April 2025, employees of a small office in the US State Department got the email many of them had been dreading.  For months, Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency had been cutting a wide swath through…
summary: The US State Department received an email regarding cuts by Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency, which had been making significant changes. This move was part of a larger effort to implement policies related to a vast censorship network. The ideas behind this network originated from the online fringe and gained traction to become part of Trump policy.

title: Made by Google 2026: all the Pixel news and announcements
content:
Google is gearing up to reveal a bunch of new Pixel devices on August 12th. A series of leaks leading up to the event suggest that the Pixel 11 lineup will come in an array of colors, with signs pointing to a built-in light coming to Pro models. Teasers from Google also indicate that it will show off a next-gen Pixel Fold alongside a Pixel Watch 5 in four different finishes. There might be a new Pixel Tag tracker as well.
Google may take the wraps off the new devices well ahead of its Made by Google livestream. On Google’s website, the countdown for preorders ends on August 12th at 10AM ET — eight hours before its event at 6PM ET. Comedian Trevor Noah will host this year’s show, featuring notable guests like NBA star Stephen Curry, podcaster Alex Cooper, Indian cricketer Shubman Gill, and Japanese actress Ayami Nakajo. We’ll be live blogging the event, so stay tuned!
Follow along for all the latest news about Google’s Pixel devices.


					
Google’s upcoming Pixel phones are for the fans, even if its launch event isn’t
			
What to expect from Google’s 2026 Pixel hardware launch event
summary: Google is set to unveil new Pixel devices on August 12th, including the Pixel 11 lineup, a next-gen Pixel Fold, and a Pixel Watch 5. The devices may be available for preorder ahead of the official livestream. The event will feature notable guests and be live blogged.

title: Mark Zuckerberg doesn’t understand how to live
content:
Recently, a man I was rock climbing with told me about how he'd used AI to make a motivational poster for himself, which he'd hung on his bedroom wall: a bear, walking a slackline over a canyon, holding a sign that said, "Do cool shit." I made what I hoped was a polite noise. What reaction was this man looking for? He probably hoped someone, maybe me, would say it was cool or inspiring. It seemed I was not the first person he'd told about this poster. "You know, it's funny," he said to me. "No one ever says anything about it." 
I have been thinking about this now for several days. There's a sort of turducken of things that I find off-puttin …
Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: A man created a motivational poster using AI, which he hung on his bedroom wall, but received little reaction from others, leading the author to ponder the significance of this event. The poster featured a bear on a slackline holding a sign that said 'Do cool shit'. The author is reflecting on the story and its implications.

title: Reddit signals ominous upcoming "changes” for old.reddit.com
content: Reddit says the beloved site is used for some "bad behavior."
summary: Reddit announced upcoming changes to old.reddit.com, citing its use for bad behavior, although the nature of these changes is not specified. The community is awaiting further details on what this means for the platform. The changes may impact user experience and moderation.

title: SpaceX spooks investors with debut earnings report
content: Shares slide in pre-market trading even as group says its quarterly revenues nearly doubled.
summary: SpaceX's debut earnings report has caused investors to become cautious, with shares sliding in pre-market trading despite the company's quarterly revenues nearly doubling. This reaction may be due to concerns over the company's financials and future growth prospects. The report's impact on investor confidence is noteworthy, but not directly related to AI or crypto.

title: White House vows to get CLARITY across ‘finish line’ in September
content: Patrick Witt says the Trump administration will keep negotiating with Democrats as the Senate prepares for a September CLARITY vote.
summary: The White House plans to continue negotiating with Democrats to pass the CLARITY act by September. The Senate is preparing for a vote on the act next month. The outcome of the negotiations and vote are still uncertain.

title: Why your Amazon order confirmation emails have become so unhelpful
content:
Earlier this summer, Amazon customers began noticing that emails related to their online orders looked sparse: Order confirmation emails didn't name specific items anymore, and instead listed only item categories. 
"Your Beauty item is confirmed!" an email about my retainer cleaning tablets read. Shoppers have posted other iterations of the redacted emails as well: "Ordered: 1 Hardware item," "Your Drugstore, Shoes, and other items are here!" and "1 Nutrition & Wellness, 1 Wireless Accessories," for example. The emails have clip art-style illustrations of general product categories, and a shopper has to exit their email and go to Amazon to  …
Read the full story at The Verge.
summary: Amazon order confirmation emails have become less detailed, no longer listing specific items, and instead categorize products, requiring customers to visit the website for more information. This change has been noticed by customers since summer. The emails now include generic category names and clip art-style illustrations.
